title: Install Nessus on Windows Server 2022
description: Build a Nessus 10.12.5 scanner on Windows Server 2022, one small step at a time. We’ll check the service, open its web page safely and make sure it is ready for the scanning class.
baseline: Nessus 10.12.5 · Windows Server 2022 with Desktop Experience · a separate practice scanner
prerequisite: Let’s set Nessus up on its own Windows Server practice VM. We’ll use the normal Windows desktop, work through the installer together, and then check the web page. Have these things ready before you begin.

lessons.title: Prepare the Windows Server 2022 Scanner
lessons.description: Let’s choose a Windows computer with enough room to run our scanner.
lessons.what: Before we install anything, let’s get our practice computer ready. Nessus will live on this computer. Later, it will check two other practice computers, which we call targets.
lessons.why: Giving Nessus enough memory and disk space now saves us from confusing failures later. We also need the Windows version with a desktop, so you can follow the clicks in this class.

steps.title: Check the supported Windows edition
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest · Start menu and System Information
actions: Let’s use a separate Windows Server 2022 x64 practice VM. Choose Desktop Experience, which gives you the Windows desktop used in our clicks. Server Core doesn’t provide that desktop and is not supported for this build. Don’t reuse a company domain controller.
Click Start, type System Information, and open the matching app. Find OS Name, Version and System Type. Write down what your own machine shows.

Need to create the VM first? In VMware Workstation Pro, click File → New Virtual Machine. Attach your permitted Server 2022 ISO, which is the installation-disc image. Install Desktop Experience on a new blank virtual disk and finish Windows setup before continuing.
steps.expected: You can identify the Windows edition and 64-bit system type on your own VM.

screenshot.title: Windows Server 2022 System Information: OS Name and System Type
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Windows Server 2022 System Information: OS Name and System Type. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

steps.title: Reserve scanner resources
steps.where: Windows host · VMware Workstation Pro > VM Settings
actions: Shut down Windows inside the practice VM first. In Workstation, select this VM and click Edit virtual machine settings. We’re changing the VM’s settings, not the hardware inside your physical computer.

For our small lab, you can use four virtual CPU cores, 8 GB RAM and a new disk of at least 80 GB. CPU cores do the processing, RAM is the computer’s working space, and the disk keeps files. Leave enough for your main computer and the two targets too. These are lab allocations, not a promise about every workload.
Start the VM. Open File Explorer → This PC and check the free space on C:. Plan for at least 30 GB for Nessus in addition to Windows, space for reports and logs, and 5 GB of temporary space.
steps.expected: Your practice VM has the planned resources, and your physical computer still has enough left for its own work.

screenshot.title: Workstation scanner VM hardware and Windows free disk space
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Workstation scanner VM hardware and Windows free disk space. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

bestPractices: Keep this scanner separate from the two computers it will scan. That makes it easier to tell each computer’s job apart.
Use supported Windows updates and a scanner installer that you are allowed to use.
commonMistakes: Server Core may look lighter, but it is not the supported desktop build we need here.
Don’t give the VM all your physical computer’s memory. Your main Windows computer still needs room to work.

troubleshooting.problem: I don’t see a Windows desktop
troubleshooting.fix: Check which edition you installed. Rebuild this practice VM with Desktop Experience if you selected Core. Installing IIS won’t turn Core into the supported desktop build.

troubleshooting.problem: My own computer is very slow
troubleshooting.fix: Check how many VMs are running and how much memory is free. Close extra VMs or use a host with enough resources; don’t carry on while the host is struggling.

quiz.question: Which server edition is suitable here?
options: Any version as long as it has a web browser
quiz.explanation: Nessus supports Server 2022 x64 but not Server Core.

quiz.question: What belongs in your disk plan?
options: The OS, Nessus, plugins, results, logs and temporary space
quiz.explanation: The installer is just one part of the storage need.

lessons.exercise: Make a small checklist for your scanner. Write its VM name, Windows edition, CPU cores, memory and free disk space. If a word is new, use the explanations in the steps.
lessons.pass: You’re ready to continue when your separate scanner VM runs a supported Windows edition and your resource checklist meets the lab plan.
needs: Open VMware Workstation Pro on your own computer. Have the Server 2022 installation ISO ready if you still need to build the practice VM.

lessons.title: Prepare Networking and the Installer
lessons.description: Let’s check the scanner’s address and make sure we have the right installer.
lessons.what: We’ll find our scanner’s name and private address, then check the file we plan to install. Think of this as checking the address and label on a delivery before opening the box.
lessons.why: You need to know which computer you’re working on. Checking the installer also helps us catch the wrong Nessus product or a file that changed on the way to you.

steps.title: Check the private scan path
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest · PowerShell
actions: First, check that your scanner and the two permitted targets use the isolated private VMnet from your lab plan. VMnet is VMware’s virtual network. Keep their actual addresses in your notes; those addresses are our practice boundary.
Open PowerShell and run the inspection lines below. Compare the computer name, address and DNS servers with your plan. DNS is the service that turns names into addresses.

If the name or address needs changing, open Server Manager → Local Server. Click Computer name or Ethernet to reach the matching settings. Use your own unused address, subnet, gateway and DNS from the plan. Restart after changing the computer name, then check again.

Our VMs may use NAT to reach the Internet for updates, but let them scan each other directly using their private addresses. Don’t send target scans through address translation; it can change what the scanner sees.

breakdown.meaning: Prints the local computer name.
Shows network adapters, addresses and gateways without changing them.
Lists configured DNS servers.
Limits the DNS display to IPv4 settings.

steps.expected: Your notes match the scanner’s current name, address and DNS settings.

screenshot.title: PowerShell actual hostname, IPv4 address and DNS configuration
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: PowerShell actual hostname, IPv4 address and DNS configuration. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

steps.title: Verify the Windows x64 Nessus MSI
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest · File Explorer and PowerShell
actions: Let’s get the correct file: the Nessus 10.12.5 Windows x64 scanner MSI from Tenable or the person responsible for your lab software. Nessus Agent is a different product. Keep the installer in your private lab folder, outside the Git repository.

In File Explorer, turn on View → File name extensions. Right-click the MSI → Properties. Look at Details and Digital Signatures. Check the version and Tenable’s signer. If either is wrong or untrusted, stop and get a verified copy.

Run the lines below and enter the installer’s real full path when asked. If Tenable publishes a separate SHA256 checksum, compare it with your result. A checksum helps detect a changed file; it does not, by itself, prove who made it.
steps.command:
$MsiPath = Read-Host 'Full path to your verified Nessus 10.12.5 x64 MSI'
Get-AuthenticodeSignature -FilePath $MsiPath | Format-List Status,SignerCertificate
Get-FileHash -Path $MsiPath -Algorithm SHA256

breakdown.meaning: Stores the path you type; it is not a password.
Asks you for a value instead of assuming a filename.
Checks the Windows digital signature. Investigate any status other than Valid.
Displays the named properties in a readable list.
Computes a file fingerprint for comparison with a trusted source.

steps.expected: You have checked the real scanner MSI’s product, version and trust information.

screenshot.title: MSI Properties and signature status; no license keys visible
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: MSI Properties and signature status; no license keys visible. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

bestPractices: Keep the installer’s actual filename and check its real product information. Renaming a different MSI doesn’t make it the right installer.
Use a private lab network that doesn’t overlap your home or VPN address ranges. Keep the management page off the public Internet.
commonMistakes: Nessus Agent and the Nessus scanner do different jobs. Double-check the product before installing.
A correct-looking filename is only a label. Check where the file came from and its signature too.

troubleshooting.problem: The signature doesn’t say Valid
troubleshooting.fix: Check the download source, your computer’s clock and certificate trust. Get a verified replacement if the problem remains unexplained; don’t click through it.

troubleshooting.problem: My VPN uses the same address range
troubleshooting.fix: Pause here. Work with the lab owner to choose a different, non-overlapping private range before you start any scan.

quiz.question: Does a SHA256 value by itself prove the file came from Tenable?
options: No; compare it with a trusted official value and verify the signer
Only if the filename includes Nessus
quiz.explanation: A hash identifies bytes. A trusted reference and signature establish more useful provenance.

quiz.question: Which traffic should use the private lab path?
options: Scanning your two authorized target VMs
Scanning every address your host can reach
quiz.explanation: Scope and direct private connectivity make this a controlled exercise.

lessons.exercise: Write down the MSI filename and verified version. Draw a simple line from the scanner to each target and label it with the real private addresses from your lab.
lessons.pass: You can point to the scanner’s private address and show that the installer is the trusted Nessus 10.12.5 Windows x64 scanner package.
needs: Start the prepared scanner VM. Keep your private network plan and verified Nessus scanner MSI nearby.

lessons.title: Install Nessus with the MSI
lessons.description: We’ll walk through the installer together and leave IIS out of this build.
lessons.what: Now we can put Nessus on the Windows server. We’ll use the installer you just checked and work through its pages one at a time.
lessons.why: Nessus brings its own secure web page. You don’t need to add IIS to make it work. We’ll teach IIS separately when we build websites.

steps.title: Run the approved installer
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest · File Explorer
actions: Sign in to the practice server with an account allowed to install software. Close other installers. Make sure this is the fresh scanner VM, with no running Nessus scans or existing Nessus/Agent installation that you could disturb.
Double-click the verified Nessus 10.12.5 x64 scanner MSI. If User Account Control appears, check the signer and confirm it is the installer you meant to open before allowing it.
At the InstallShield Welcome page, click Next. Read the license agreement. Accept it only if you are allowed to do so, then click Next.
steps.expected: The verified Nessus installer has reached its setup pages.

screenshot.title: Nessus InstallShield Welcome and approved destination folder
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Nessus InstallShield Welcome and approved destination folder. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

steps.title: Complete the installation
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest · Nessus InstallShield Wizard
actions: Keep the suggested installation folder unless your lab has a specific approved folder to use. Click Next, then Install.
Give the installer time to finish; don’t open a second copy. If it asks for a restart, save your work and restart the practice VM. When the completion page appears, click Finish.
Write down the actual result. Leave the IIS Web Server role alone—Nessus already has its own web server. Even if your browser opens automatically, let’s check the service in the next lesson.
steps.expected: The installer reports its actual result, and any requested restart has finished.

screenshot.title: Nessus InstallShield completion page; omit any private data
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Nessus InstallShield completion page; omit any private data. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

bestPractices: Use a practice practice VM for this class. A company server needs its agreed change and maintenance process.
Keep the verified installer in your private software folder in case an approved repair needs it later.
commonMistakes: A browser-based page does not mean an application needs IIS. Nessus already has its own web server.
Don’t install over a working scanner or a different Nessus product just to get through the wizard. You could interrupt work or lose scan data.

troubleshooting.problem: The installer asks me to restart
troubleshooting.fix: Save your work and restart the practice VM normally. Then continue by checking Services.

troubleshooting.problem: The installer fails
troubleshooting.fix: Keep the exact message. Open Event Viewer → Windows Logs → Application and look for the matching Windows Installer event. Fix that cause before retrying.

quiz.question: Does Nessus need IIS for its web interface?
options: No, Nessus provides its own web server
quiz.explanation: IIS application hosting is separate from Nessus installation.

quiz.question: What do you do after a requested restart?
options: Restart safely and then verify the Nessus service
quiz.explanation: Complete the operating-system change before checking the service.

lessons.exercise: Complete the installer and write down what it actually says at the end. If it asks for a restart, restart the practice server before moving on.
lessons.pass: The Nessus installer finishes successfully and you have completed any restart it requested.
needs: Finish the installer and network checks first. Sign in with an account allowed to install software on this practice VM.

lessons.title: Manage the Nessus Windows Service
lessons.description: Find the background helper that keeps Nessus running.
lessons.what: Let’s meet the Tenable Nessus service. A service is a program that can keep working in the background, even when you close its window.
lessons.why: The browser page depends on this helper. If the service is stopped, clicking Refresh in the browser won’t start the scanner for you.

steps.title: Find the installed service
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest · Services
actions: Press Windows+R. Type services.msc and press Enter. In the list, look for the display name Tenable Nessus.
Open its Properties. Read the service status and startup type, then write down what you see. We’ll use the documented display name instead of guessing another service name.
If the service is stopped, right-click Tenable Nessus → Start using your permitted administrator account. Refresh the list and check the result.
steps.expected: You can see Tenable Nessus and explain its current service state.

screenshot.title: Services row and Properties for Tenable Nessus
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Services row and Properties for Tenable Nessus. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

steps.title: Use the documented service commands
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest · elevated PowerShell
actions: Right-click PowerShell and choose Run as administrator. Run the first line below to ask Windows for the service’s status.
If it is stopped, use the documented net start line below. If it is already running, you don’t need to start it again. Don’t stop a working service just to try the button; that can interrupt scans.

When you have an approved reason to stop it for maintenance, use net stop "Tenable Nessus". Start it again when the work is finished and check its status. Starting the service does not automatically restart an interrupted scan.

breakdown.meaning: Reads Windows service status.
Looks up the friendly name shown in Services.
Starts a Windows service; it does not install the product.
Quotes preserve the spaces in this service’s display name.

steps.expected: The service query and Services window agree, or you have an error to investigate.

screenshot.title: Elevated PowerShell service query and actual result
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Elevated PowerShell service query and actual result. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

bestPractices: Look for running scans before planning a service stop. A background service may be doing work even when its page is closed.
Use administrator rights when a task needs them. Simply viewing the Nessus page does not require an administrator Windows session.
commonMistakes: Refreshing the browser won’t start a stopped service. Check Services first.
Use Tenable Nessus, not a guessed name or the Nessus Agent service.

troubleshooting.problem: Tenable Nessus is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Return to the installation result. Check that you installed the scanner MSI and completed any requested restart.

troubleshooting.problem: It starts and stops right away
troubleshooting.fix: Read the service error, Windows events and Nessus logs. Check available disk space before trying repeated restarts.

quiz.question: Which friendly service name should you find?
quiz.explanation: The Nessus scanner has its own Windows service.

quiz.question: What should you check before stopping it?
options: Whether scans are active and maintenance is approved
Only whether the browser is closed
quiz.explanation: Stopping the scanner can interrupt work and affect results.

lessons.exercise: Find Tenable Nessus in Services. Then use the PowerShell check to show the same service status in a second way.
lessons.pass: You can find the right Nessus service, explain whether it is running, and investigate any error instead of guessing.
needs: Finish the Nessus installation and any restart it requested. We’ll use Services and an administrator PowerShell window.

lessons.title: Allow Only Approved Access on Port 8834
lessons.description: Let your administration computer reach Nessus without opening the door to everyone.
lessons.what: The firewall is like a door guard. We’ll tell it which computer may use the Nessus management page and which numbered door, called a port, that page uses.
lessons.why: Nessus may hold private reports and stored scan credentials. We want you to reach its page, but we don’t want every computer on a network to have the same invitation.

steps.title: Identify the active profile and administrator address
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest · PowerShell and Windows Defender Firewall
actions: Find the exact IPv4 address of the computer you’ll use to open the Nessus page. This is your administration computer’s address, not a scan target’s address. Use the address in your lab plan.
Run the inspection line below. Then press Windows+R, type wf.msc and press Enter to open Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security. Read which network profile is active.

Check that the active profile matches your private lab plan. If it unexpectedly says Public, or a company policy manages the firewall, pause and have the owner review it. Don’t turn the firewall off to get past this check.

breakdown.meaning: Shows each connected network and its category; it does not change the network.

steps.expected: You know the active network profile and the one administration address this rule should allow.

screenshot.title: Firewall overview active profile and PowerShell connection profile
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Firewall overview active profile and PowerShell connection profile. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

steps.title: Create and inspect the restricted rule
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest · elevated PowerShell
actions: The example below is for a lab that has approved Private or Domain profiles. If your network uses a different profile, get the correct rule agreed before running it.
When asked, enter your administration computer’s real IPv4 address. Run the rule-creation line once. The RemoteAddress must be that address, not Any.

In wf.msc, open Inbound Rules → SONIC Nessus UI from admin. Check Protocols and Ports, Scope → Remote IP addresses, and Advanced → Profiles. Review any older wide-open Nessus rules too. A narrow new rule does not cancel a second rule that still allows everyone; only restrict or remove one after checking the lab’s approved plan.
steps.command:
$AdminIP = Read-Host 'Approved administrator IPv4 address'
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'SONIC Nessus UI from admin' -Direction Inbound -Action Allow -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 8834 -RemoteAddress $AdminIP -Profile Private,Domain

breakdown.meaning: Stores the trusted source address you enter.
Creates one Windows firewall rule; check existing rules too.
Allows matching traffic arriving at the scanner.
Matches the Nessus HTTPS management port.
Restricts the source to your administrator computer.
Makes the rule apply only to the listed approved network categories.

steps.expected: Your rule matches the intended profile, TCP8834 and administration source. You have also checked for wider rules.

screenshot.title: Firewall rule Protocols and Ports, Scope and Profile tabs
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Firewall rule Protocols and Ports, Scope and Profile tabs. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

bestPractices: Leave Windows Defender Firewall on. We only need a specific permitted path to the scanner.
Port 8834 opens the scanner’s management page. Target logins and scans use other protocols with their own rules.
commonMistakes: The management rule belongs on the scanner. Opening 8834 on every target does not solve scanner-page access.
Check for a second wide-open rule. One narrow rule does not cancel another rule that still allows Any source.

troubleshooting.problem: I made the rule, but the page is still unreachable
troubleshooting.fix: Compare the active profile, administration address, scanner address and listening service. A domain policy can override a local rule.

troubleshooting.problem: I see duplicate rules
troubleshooting.fix: Check their names, scope and purpose first. Only disable the course-created duplicate after checking that it is safe to do so.

quiz.question: Who should be allowed to browse TCP8834 in this exercise?
options: Every unknown device on the LAN
quiz.explanation: Management access is restricted to the approved source.

quiz.question: Does creating a narrow rule automatically cancel every broad allow rule?
options: Only if it has SONIC in its name
quiz.explanation: Other matching allow rules may still permit access.

lessons.exercise: Open the rule you created. Show its TCP port, the allowed source address and its network profile. Explain why a second, wider rule could spoil the restriction.
lessons.pass: Your Nessus management rule allows the intended administration computer, and you have checked for other rules that allow more access.
needs: Write down the administration computer’s real IPv4 address. Know which private network profile your lab is using.

lessons.title: Open the Nessus HTTPS Console
lessons.description: Open the scanner’s welcome page and check that you reached the right computer.
lessons.what: We’ll open Nessus first on the scanner itself, then from your normal administration computer. The secure web address starts with https:// and ends with :8834.
lessons.why: This gives us two useful checks. Local access tells us about the scanner’s own page. Remote access also tests the network path and firewall rule.

steps.title: Test the local web listener first
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest · browser
actions: On the scanner VM itself, open a browser and type https://localhost:8834. Localhost means this same computer. Keep both https:// and :8834 in the address.

A new Nessus installation uses a self-signed certificate, so your browser may show a warning. Read it and check that you really are on your own scanner. Don’t treat every certificate warning as harmless.

For this isolated first-time lab, use the browser’s advanced/continue option only if your lab rules allow that exception. If policy blocks it, use the approved certificate process instead of switching off browser checks.
steps.expected: You reach your own scanner’s welcome page locally, or you have a clear local error to investigate.

screenshot.title: Browser address bar and Nessus welcome page; no private fields entered
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Browser address bar and Nessus welcome page; no private fields entered. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

steps.title: Test from the administrator workstation
steps.where: Approved Windows administrator workstation · PowerShell and browser
actions: Back on your administration computer, run the test below and enter the scanner’s real private IPv4 address. This tests the TCP connection; it doesn’t check the license or plugins.
In its browser, open https://YOUR-SCANNER-PRIVATE-IP:8834. Replace the words with the scanner address from your notes; don’t type the placeholder literally.
Check the certificate and intended scanner identity before using any permitted lab exception. If the page worked locally but not here, start by checking the private network path and firewall rule.

breakdown.meaning: Tests a connection from this Windows computer.
Uses the scanner destination you entered.
Tests the scanner management TCP port.
True means TCP connected; it does not prove TLS trust, licensing or plugin readiness.

steps.expected: You understand whether the remote TCP test and browser connection passed, and what any certificate warning means.

screenshot.title: Administrator workstation private scanner URL and connectivity test
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Administrator workstation private scanner URL and connectivity test. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

bestPractices: Use the scanner’s correct private name or address. Check the identity before entering a password or activation code.
A temporary setup exception is only for the permitted isolated lab. Use approved trusted certificates for company access.
commonMistakes: Check the address carefully: https://, the scanner address, then :8834. Don’t browse a target by mistake.
A successful TCP test proves a connection, not that the web certificate is trusted.

troubleshooting.problem: Even localhost won’t open
troubleshooting.fix: Check the Tenable Nessus service and whether anything is listening locally on 8834.

troubleshooting.problem: Localhost works, but the other computer cannot connect
troubleshooting.fix: Check the private VMnet, current addresses, route and source-limited firewall rule before changing Nessus settings.

quiz.question: Which URL format reaches local Nessus?
quiz.explanation: The default web interface uses HTTPS on TCP8834.

quiz.question: What does a successful TCP test prove?
options: Only that a TCP connection could be made
That all scan plugins are current
quiz.explanation: Licensing and application readiness require separate checks.

lessons.exercise: Open the intended Nessus welcome page in both places. Describe any certificate warning and why you did or did not continue in this isolated lab.
lessons.pass: You understand both connection results. Any temporary certificate exception is limited to this lab and follows your lab’s rules.
needs: Check that the Tenable Nessus service is running. Have the scanner’s private address and your browser ready.

lessons.title: Activate Nessus and Initialize Plugins
lessons.description: Choose your licensed Nessus product and wait for its checks to become ready.
lessons.what: Nessus needs its license and its plugins before it can do useful work. Plugins are small checks, like items on an inspector’s checklist.
lessons.why: A running service is only part of the job. The license decides which features you may use, and the plugins need to finish loading before we start a scan.

steps.title: Choose the approved activation route
steps.where: Nessus browser console · Welcome/setup pages
actions: At the Welcome page, choose the product and registration route your actual license allows. The license is your permission to use a particular product and set of features. Don’t pick Professional, Expert, Essentials or Security Center-managed just because the name looks familiar.

For your licensed online standalone product, follow its setup wizard and enter activation details directly in the real Nessus page. Make a unique Nessus administrator account. This is a separate login from the Windows Administrator account.

Save the code and password in your approved password manager. Leave them out of notes, screenshots, terminal history and GitHub. If you don’t know which product your license permits, check with your instructor before continuing.
steps.expected: You have selected the product your license permits and protected the new Nessus login.

screenshot.title: Product selection/setup screen with all activation and password fields hidden
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Product selection/setup screen with all activation and password fields hidden. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

steps.title: Wait for and verify plugin initialization
steps.where: Nessus browser console · initialization and Settings/About
actions: Let the plugins download and compile, which means Nessus is preparing its checks for use. Keep the VM on and make sure it has free disk space. There isn’t one waiting time that fits every computer.

When you can sign in, open Settings → About, or the matching page in your version. Record the actual Nessus version, licensed product and plugin-set date or readiness. Keep activation codes out of the record.

Using an offline lab? Use Register Offline only if your license supports it, and follow Tenable’s two-computer instructions. Essentials does not support offline installation. Keep the private license file outside this repository. For Nessus 10.12.5, a manual plugin update also needs its matching signature file. A .tar.gz filename alone doesn’t tell us what is inside it.
steps.expected: Your own console shows the installed product, version and plugin status, or you have clearly recorded what is still loading or blocked.

screenshot.title: Ready console and version/plugin information with license identifiers redacted
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Ready console and version/plugin information with license identifiers redacted. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

bestPractices: Treat application updates and plugin updates as separate tasks. They do not change the same thing.
Use the current signed offline-update process when it applies. Don’t try to bypass a signature check to force a file to load.
commonMistakes: Choose the product your license permits, not whichever name sounds familiar.
Keep the VM running while plugins prepare. Ready plugins also don’t mean that every template is included in your license.

troubleshooting.problem: The download cannot connect
troubleshooting.fix: Check DNS, the clock, your approved proxy and the permitted feed connection. Keep the exact message so you can check the right cause.

troubleshooting.problem: An offline file is rejected
troubleshooting.fix: Check which scanner and product the license belongs to, where the files came from, and whether the required signature matches. Ask the software owner for help; don’t rename random files to make them fit.

quiz.question: Is your Nessus administrator automatically your Windows Administrator?
options: No; it is a separate application account
quiz.explanation: The accounts belong to different security systems.

quiz.question: Can a 10.12.5 manual plugin import rely on an unsigned archive alone?
options: No; the supported signed update package/workflow is required
Yes, if you disable certificate checks
quiz.explanation: The 10.12.5 release requires a signature file for manual scanner plugin updates.

lessons.exercise: Write down the product name, actual installed version and plugin readiness. Leave activation codes and passwords out of your evidence.
lessons.pass: You have checked the licensed product and ready plugins in the real console without exposing a secret.
needs: Reach the intended Nessus welcome page. Have your licensed product name and private activation method ready.

lessons.title: Configure Trusted HTTPS Access
lessons.description: Give the Nessus web page an identity your browser can check.
lessons.what: Let’s look at the web page’s certificate. It is an identity card for the server. We’ll prepare the correct files and, when you have permission, install them and check the result.
lessons.why: A browser warning is a clue to investigate. In a company environment, repeatedly clicking past warnings is not a good way to decide who you are talking to.

steps.title: Plan the certificate and rollback
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest · secure administrator workspace
actions: Choose the DNS name you’ll type to reach Nessus. Ask the person providing the certificate for a server certificate with that name in its Subject Alternative Name, or SAN. If you will browse by IP too, that IP must be covered as well.

Get the matching server key, server certificate and certificate-authority chain through your approved process. The key is private. Keep the files in a protected local folder, not in a shared class folder or Git checkout.

Before changing the certificate, arrange a maintenance time and check that no scans are running. Back up the current certificate and key privately, and write down how to restore them. If you don’t have the files or permission yet, complete a clearly labeled preparation plan; don’t call the import finished.
steps.expected: You have the approved matching files and recovery plan, or a specific list of what is still missing.

screenshot.title: Certificate public Details tab showing SAN; never show private key contents
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Certificate public Details tab showing SAN; never show private key contents. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

steps.title: Import and verify only approved matching files
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest · elevated PowerShell
actions: Check that you have the matching files before using import-certs. Enter their local paths below, not their contents. The paths must point to the matching unencrypted PEM server key, server certificate and CA certificate required by Tenable’s procedure.

Stop the service only during the agreed maintenance time. Import the files and read the result before starting it again. If validation fails, stop and investigate the message; don’t try to force it by copying random files over the originals.

Open Nessus using the DNS name that matches the certificate. Check the certificate chain, name and expiry. If access or trust breaks, follow the recovery plan you wrote down. A freshly made self-signed certificate does not automatically become trusted by every browser.
steps.command:
$KeyPath = Read-Host 'Protected server key PEM path'
$CertPath = Read-Host 'Server certificate PEM path'
$CaPath = Read-Host 'CA certificate PEM path'
net stop "Tenable Nessus"
& 'C:\Program Files\Tenable\Nessus\nessuscli.exe' import-certs "--serverkey=$KeyPath" "--servercert=$CertPath" "--cacert=$CaPath"
net start "Tenable Nessus"

breakdown.meaning: Asks for local file paths, not certificate or key contents.
PowerShell call operator: runs the quoted executable path.
Default Nessus administration tool location; use the real installation path if approved custom setup differs.
Validates and installs the matching certificate material.
Identify the private key, public server certificate and CA certificate files.
Creates a maintenance interruption; only run during the approved window.

steps.expected: The approved name opens with the expected certificate chain, or you have recorded the failure and followed your recovery plan.

screenshot.title: Browser certificate chain, SAN and expiry after approved import
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Browser certificate chain, SAN and expiry after approved import. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

bestPractices: Follow the certificate owner’s requirements, including which certificate chain to use and who may read the private key.
Keep production private keys out of this class and all certificate/key files out of SONIC-Academy uploads.
commonMistakes: A certificate for a different name will still give a name error. Check its SAN, not just the filename.
Making a certificate with mkcert does not automatically make every computer trust it.

troubleshooting.problem: The browser still reports a name mismatch
troubleshooting.fix: Compare the address you typed with the certificate’s SAN. Fix the DNS record or use the correct covered name, or obtain a corrected certificate.

troubleshooting.problem: The service or secure page breaks
troubleshooting.fix: Use your private backup and recorded recovery plan. Check the service and browser again after restoring the approved configuration.

quiz.question: Which certificate field must match the browser name?
quiz.explanation: Modern browser checks depend on the SAN matching the access name/IP.

quiz.question: Where does the server private key belong?
options: In an approved protected local location
quiz.explanation: Private keys are secrets and need restricted access.

lessons.exercise: If you have the approved matching files, complete the import and verify trusted access. If you don’t, list exactly what is missing and leave the import marked as not performed.
lessons.pass: You have either verified the approved trusted connection or clearly recorded the missing files or permission. A preparation plan does not count as a successful certificate import.
needs: Have the approved server name, matching certificate files and a private recovery copy. If any are missing, we can complete the preparation plan first.

lessons.title: Troubleshoot Service and Connection Problems
lessons.description: Work out which part is failing before changing settings.
lessons.what: When the Nessus page won’t open, we’ll check one part at a time: the service, the listening port, the network path, and the certificate.
lessons.why: This is like checking a lamp, its cord and its outlet. Changing everything at once makes it harder to find the real cause and harder to undo your changes.

steps.title: Inspect service, listener and application events
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest · elevated PowerShell and Event Viewer
actions: Run the checks below and compare the service status with the listening TCP8834 port. Even a running service may still be preparing plugins, so read the actual messages too.
Open Event Viewer → Windows Logs → Application and System. Look around the time the problem happened for Nessus, service or Windows Installer events.

In File Explorer’s address bar, enter C:\ProgramData\Tenable\Nessus\nessus\logs. ProgramData may be hidden, but typing the path can still open it. Read nessusd.messages and www_server.log near the error time. If your installation uses a custom location, check Tenable’s Manage Logs page. Keep useful timestamps and disk information in your notes, and remove credentials and private target details before sharing logs.
steps.command:
Get-Service -DisplayName 'Tenable Nessus'
Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8834 -State Listen -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Get-Volume -DriveLetter C

breakdown.meaning: Lists actual TCP endpoints on this computer.
Filters to listeners on the Nessus management port.
Suppresses the no-match error display; an empty list still means no matching listener was found.
Shows capacity and free space on the C volume.

steps.expected: You have service, listener, storage or log saved result that helps narrow the problem.

screenshot.title: Service/listener query and a relevant redacted event
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Service/listener query and a relevant redacted event. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

steps.title: Separate remote TCP failure from HTTPS trust failure
steps.where: Approved administrator workstation · PowerShell and browser
actions: Test the scanner’s private IP on TCP8834 again. If local access works but this test fails, compare the VMnet, current addresses, firewall source address and network profile.

If TCP works but the browser rejects the page, check the https:// address, certificate name, certificate chain, expiry and your computer’s clock. These are different checks from opening a firewall port.

If the page opens but plugins aren’t ready, check the update status and permitted outbound feed or proxy path. Fix one cause you have saved result for, then test again. Don’t switch off the firewall, UAC, antivirus or TLS checks as a general cure.

breakdown.meaning: Checks network reachability from the actual administrator workstation; it does not check browser trust.

steps.expected: You can distinguish a network problem from a web-identity or plugin problem, then test one supported correction.

screenshot.title: Browser exact error and matching TCP test with private details redacted
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Browser exact error and matching TCP test with private details redacted. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

bestPractices: Try one explained change at a time and keep the earlier settings so you can return to them.
After a practice troubleshooting change, restore the agreed working setup and test again.
commonMistakes: Ping and HTTPS are different checks. A failed ping alone does not tell you whether the Nessus page can open.
Check the service, listening port and destination before reaching for the installer again.

troubleshooting.problem: There is no service or listening port
troubleshooting.fix: Go back to the installation and service checks. Repeated browser reloads cannot create the missing service.

troubleshooting.problem: I only see a certificate error
troubleshooting.fix: Check the server identity, clock and certificate chain. A wider firewall rule won’t fix a certificate problem.

quiz.question: Local Nessus works but remote TCP8834 fails. What is a sensible next check?
options: VMnet, address and source-scoped firewall rules
quiz.explanation: The local application works; check the remote network path.

quiz.question: TCP8834 connects but the browser reports a name mismatch. Which layer needs attention?
quiz.explanation: A certificate-name problem is different from a blocked TCP port.

lessons.exercise: Follow the checks using a real problem you encounter. If everything works, talk through a clearly labeled pretend problem instead of breaking the server to create one.
lessons.pass: You can explain which part is failing, show the saved result, and try one permitted correction before testing again.
needs: Keep the scanner console and administration computer available. Write down the time and exact message of the problem you are checking.

lessons.title: Validate the Completed Windows Installation
lessons.description: Let’s check the whole installation before we call the scanner ready.
lessons.what: We’ll collect a few real checks that show the scanner is ready for the next class. An installer completion message alone doesn’t tell us that everything else works.
lessons.why: Someone else should be able to read your notes and understand what works, what you tested, and what still needs attention.

steps.title: Complete the installation evidence checklist
steps.where: Windows Server 2022 guest and approved administrator browser
actions: Let’s tick off the real installation checks: Windows edition, installed Nessus version 10.12.5, licensed product, Tenable Nessus service Running, and completed plugin preparation. Use what your own screens show.
Check both local and administration-computer HTTPS access. Review the web certificate, who can pass the firewall rule, the update method and plugin-set status.

Open the available templates only to see what your license offers. We aren’t launching a scan in this installation class. Don’t assume reporting or compliance features are included. Hide license identifiers before capturing any screen.
steps.expected: Each readiness item has a real result instead of a guess.

screenshot.title: Nessus About/version and ready console with license identifiers hidden
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Nessus About/version and ready console with license identifiers hidden. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

steps.title: Record the handoff and secure stored materials
steps.where: Secure lab notes · no secrets in SONIC-Academy
actions: Write a small handoff note: scanner name and private address, who owns it, who to contact for help, update method, maintenance time and where the recovery instructions are stored. Keep passwords and licenses in the separate approved vault.
Add screenshots from your own lab only after hiding private information. The course’s capture checklist is a reminder of what to photograph, not saved result that you already did the work.

If a readiness check failed, fix it or leave it clearly unfinished before moving to the scanning class. Remember that Nessus does the scanning; Tenable Security Center is a separate management product that a standalone license does not automatically include.
steps.expected: Your handoff notes explain what works, what still needs attention and where private material is kept safely.

screenshot.title: Redacted readiness/handoff checklist; no license or password contents
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Redacted readiness/handoff checklist; no license or password contents. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

bestPractices: Record values and times that you actually observed on your own computer.
A ready scanner is different from a successful authenticated target scan. We will check target access in the next class.
commonMistakes: Finishing the MSI does not finish every readiness check. Look at the service, web access and plugins too.
Before sharing an About page, check that no activation information is visible.

troubleshooting.problem: I can’t collect one of the checks
troubleshooting.fix: Leave it unfinished and write down what is missing. Don’t fill the gap with an invented screenshot or result.

troubleshooting.problem: My license shows fewer features
troubleshooting.fix: Use the features your product actually permits or arrange the right license. A missing licensed template is not automatically an installation fault.

quiz.question: Which result is sufficient by itself to prove full readiness?
options: Neither; check service, version, entitlement, plugins and access
quiz.explanation: The installation checklist covers several independent layers.

quiz.question: Is Tenable Security Center automatically included with standalone Nessus?
options: No; it is a separate management product/entitlement
quiz.explanation: Scanner installation does not grant a separate management-platform license.

lessons.exercise: Make a short readiness checklist. Mark each item passed, failed or waiting for something, and attach only screenshots that hide private information.
lessons.pass: Each required installation check has real evidence. Anything you could not check is clearly listed as unfinished.
needs: Have your service, access, license and plugin checks available. We’ll compare them with the checklist instead of starting a scan.

lessons.title: Final Practical: Build and Hand Off a Windows Scanner
lessons.description: Build your Windows scanner, then show someone how you know it is ready.
lessons.what: This is your turn to put the steps together. Use your own practice server and explain the checks as you go, as though you were showing a classmate.
lessons.why: Being able to explain what you did helps you notice gaps. We want a scanner you understand, not just a wizard you clicked through.

steps.title: Perform the installation using your own lab values
steps.where: Dedicated Windows Server 2022 Desktop Experience lab VM
actions: Start with your prepared practice VM. Check the Nessus 10.12.5 x64 scanner MSI again, then complete the installation using the private network plan you actually chose.
Check the Tenable Nessus service, limit web access to the intended administration computer, and open the correct private HTTPS page.

Activate only the product your license permits and wait for ready plugins. For offline registration, check the license and the 10.12.5 signed-update requirements before importing a file. If you can’t verify a file, stop rather than guessing.
steps.expected: Your own installation has real service, web-access and plugin checks, with unfinished items left visible.

screenshot.title: Final Windows scanner service and ready Nessus console, redacted
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Final Windows scanner service and ready Nessus console, redacted. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

steps.title: Demonstrate, explain and hand off
steps.where: Approved administrator workstation · secure evidence notes
actions: Show your instructor the installed version, licensed product, ready plugins, service status, limited web access and server identity. Describe the certificate honestly: either a permitted temporary lab exception or a verified trusted certificate chain.

Explain, in your own words, why Nessus didn’t need IIS, why we limited access to port 8834, and why a plugin archive needs its matching verified signature. Run one diagnostic check and explain what you see.
List anything still unfinished, along with the maintenance and recovery plan. We’ll launch scans only in the next course, after confirming the exact targets and scan-account permissions.
steps.expected: Another learner can follow your explanation and see the saved result without seeing your secrets.

screenshot.title: Final redacted practical checklist and handoff summary
screenshot.instructions: When you reach this screen in your own practice lab, capture: Final redacted practical checklist and handoff summary. Include the controls that helped you check the result. Hide passwords, activation codes, license contents, private keys and unrelated personal details. We still need a genuine screenshot here; this panel is your capture checklist.

bestPractices: Explain each check in your own words. If you can teach the next learner, you are more likely to understand the work.
Keep Windows, Nessus and scan-account passwords and license details in the private place chosen for the lab.
commonMistakes: Use a real screen and the actual version. A course placeholder is not saved result of your installation.
Don’t scan a random address to prove the scanner works. The next class sets the exact permitted targets first.

troubleshooting.problem: I’m missing something needed for the practical
troubleshooting.fix: List the exact missing file, permission or resource. Finish the independent checks you can actually verify, and leave the rest unfinished.

troubleshooting.problem: A check fails while I’m showing my work
troubleshooting.fix: Keep the failed result. Investigate the right part, make one permitted correction and record the new test result.

quiz.question: What should your final evidence show?
options: Actual observed readiness with secrets removed
A copied success message from another lab
quiz.explanation: Only your real lab saved result can support your completion claim.

quiz.question: What comes before the first vulnerability scan?
options: A written authorized target scope and approved scan configuration
Scanning your whole subnet to discover what is there
quiz.explanation: The next class establishes the exact permitted scan before it runs.

lessons.exercise: Hand over a working practice scanner and a short set of redacted notes, or an honest list of blocked work. Explain the network, service, web identity, license and plugin checks.
lessons.pass: Your instructor can follow the saved result and see what passed and what still needs live validation. Don’t turn an unfinished check into a success just to finish the page.
needs: Use the separate prepared Server 2022 practice VM, verified scanner installer and license route from the earlier lessons.

supplies: A separate Windows Server 2022 VM with Desktop Experience. Choose the version with a Windows desktop, not Server Core.
For this practice scanner, four virtual CPU cores, 8 GB of memory and a new disk of at least 80 GB. Keep enough resources free for your own computer too.
The verified Nessus 10.12.5 Windows x64 scanner MSI. An MSI is a Windows installer; Nessus Agent is a different product.
A Nessus license or account that permits the product and setup route you will use. Keep its activation details in your password manager.
Your private VMware lab network and the actual address of the computer you will use to open the Nessus page.
A safe place for lab notes and screenshots, separate from passwords and license files.
